title: Agonist and antagonist TRUPATH assays for G protein-coupled receptors
protocol: Remove a 10 or 15 cm dish of HEK293T cells from the cell culture incubator.
Dislodge the cells from the dish using Trypsin-EDTA and manual disruption after aspirating the cell media.
Centrifuge the cells gently.
Aspirate the media from the centrifuged cells.
Resuspend the cells and seed them into a new 10-cm tissue culture dish.
Dilute DNA in OptiMEM.
Incubate the diluted DNA with TransIT-2020 for 20 minutes.
Add the DNA complexes drop-wise to the HEK293T cells.
Return the treated cells to the tissue culture incubator for further incubation.
Aspirate tissue culture media from initial dish.
Apply enough Trypsin-EDTA to cover the cells.
Let sit for 3–5 minutes, gently agitating or tipping the dish from side-to-side.
Gently triturate cells by repeated aspiration and transfer dissociated cells to a 50 mL conical tube containing an equal or greater volume of complete DMEM.
Centrifuge cells for 5 minutes at 250 × g using a 22°C table-top centrifuge.
Aspirate the supernatant, leaving the gently pelleted cells at the bottom of the conical tube.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 1 mL of complete DMEM by gentle trituration with a 1 mL pipette.
Add 9 mL of complete DMEM and mix by gentle inversion.
Count and assess cell viability.
Gently and evenly distribute cells to a fresh 10 cm tissue culture dish containing 10–15 mL complete DMEM at a density of 6.5–7 million cells per dish.
Return the dish to the incubator.
Prepare DNA reagents for transfection 5–8 hours after plating.
Bring Opti-MEM and TransIT-2020 (protected from light) to 22°C.
Dilute DNA in Opti-MEM for each component (DRD2, G α Z-RLuc8, G β 3, and GFP2-G γ 1) to 10 ng/μL.
Combine diluted DNA at a ratio of 1:1:1:1, to achieve a total concentration of 4 μg in a final volume of 400 μL.
Add TransIT-2020 to the Opti-MEM/DNA mixture at a ratio of 3:1 (TransIT-2020:DNA).
Gently mix the mixture by flicking it.
Let DNA complexes form for 20–30 minutes.
Remove the tissue culture dish from the incubator.
Evenly distribute the DNA/TransIT-2020 mixture dropwise into the tissue culture media.
Gently mix the tissue culture dish in a slow figure eight motion.
Return the tissue culture dish to the incubator overnight.
The following day, remove the tissue culture dish from the incubator.
Transfer cells to a 384-well white tissue culture plate.
Prepare a 100 μg/mL Poly-L-Lysine solution in sterile water + 1% Pen-Strep (v/v).
Dispense 30 μL of the Poly-L-Lysine solution into each well of a 384-well plate.
Incubate the plate with the solution for 30–60 min at 37°C.
Shake out the Poly-L-Lysine from each well.
Add 30 μL of sterile H2O + 1% Pen-Strep (v/v) to each well.
Store the prepared plates wrapped and in the dark at 4°C for up to 2–3 weeks if not used immediately.
Retrieve the plate before use, shake out liquid, and let dry in a sterile hood for 1 h.
Gently centrifuge cells.
Aspirate off the media.
Resuspend and dilute cells to a density between 375 to 625 cells/μL.
Seed cells into a Poly-L-Lysine coated 384-well tissue culture plate.
Harvest cells by gently trituration using Versene to detach.
Transfer detached cells to conical tubes containing dFBS DMEM.
Spin down the cells at 250× g for 5 min.
Aspirate off the supernatant from the pellet.
Add 1 mL of 1% dFBS DMEM to the cell pellet.
Resuspend and dilute to 5 mL.
Count cells and adjust density between 375 and 625 cells/μL.
Plate 40 μL (15,000–25,000 cells) into each well of the coated 384-well plate.
Spin plates at 100× g for 15-30 seconds.
Return plates to the tissue-culture incubator.
Resuspend the drug plate by transferring 79.2 μL of drug buffer to each well.
Transfer 79.2 μL of assay buffer to each well.
Add substrate to each well according to the protocol.
Transfer compounds from the prepared drug plate to the assay plate using an Integra VIAFLO.
Perform concentration-response curves with half-log dilutions starting at a concentration of 10^-4.5 M.
Resuspend compounds using an Integra VIAFLO by transferring drug buffer to the drug plate.
Dilute Renilla Luciferase substrate in methanol to 1 mM and then dilute further in assay buffer to 7.5 μM.
Remove media from tissue culture plates manually.
Replace removed media with diluted luciferase substrate.
Add resuspended compounds to the tissue culture plate containing transfected cells and substrate.
Load the treated tissue culture plate into the plate reader for data acquisition.
Dissolve BRET2 substrate in methanol to a concentration of 1 mM.
Store the dissolved substrate in the dark on dry ice during use.
Wrap and store the remaining substrate at -80°C after the experiment.
Shake out and blot the 384-well tissue culture plate.
Place PerkinElmer white backing strips on the underside of the plate.
Dilute 75 μL of BRET2 substrate into 10 mL of assay buffer to achieve a final concentration of 7.5 μM.
Load 20 μL of solution into each well in the cell plate.
Transfer 10 μL of drugs to the cell plate using a liquid handler.
Spin the plates at 100× g for 10 seconds in a centrifuge.
Load the plate into the PHERAstar FSX.
Scan each well with a 3 mm spiral average.
Read the plate 8 times over a period of 40 minutes.
Optimize gain settings for channel A (GFP2) and channel B (RLuc8).
Export data from the plate reader for subsequent analysis.
Calculate the ratio of GFP2 signal to RLuc8 signal.
Transfer data to an X/Y plot in GraphPad Prism.
Use a 4-parameter logistic fit to calculate EC50s.
Plot EC50 values by time.
Identify the time-point where EC50 values have stabilized.
Using the average ratio-value from the minimum signal wells (DMSO only) as 0%, normalize the change in BRET ratio with compound treatment.
Use the maximum signal wells (sufficient concentration of control compound to achieve a maximal response) as 100% for normalization.
Perform a 4-parameter logistic fit regression using normalized values.
Determine the EC50 and hill-slope for the agonist stimulation condition to use as a competitor in antagonist assays.
Set the ECF to 80 for determining the effective concentration of the test agonist at EC80.
Resuspend the drug plate by transferring 79.2 μL of drug buffer to each well manually or via an automated liquid handler.
Prepare drug plates containing test compounds at desired concentrations for single-point or concentration-response assays.
Include the test agonist at an EC80 concentration in each well with the test antagonist.
Set up control wells consisting of minimum (DMSO), maximum, and EC80 concentrations of the test agonist.
Use 300 μM dopamine in 0.99% DMSO as the maximum control to achieve a final concentration of 100 μM dopamine with 0.33% DMSO.
Prepare EC80 wells containing 90 nM dopamine for a final concentration of 30 nM dopamine.
Include EC80 concentrations of test antagonists in addition to the agonist.
Use full-log dilutions of test antagonists starting at 30 μM to create the curve, achieving a final concentration of 10 μM.
Employ droperidol, Ziprasidone HCl, L741,626, and Risperidone as test antagonists in this experiment.

Store the dissolved substrate in the dark on dry ice during use and then wrap in Parafilm for storage at -80°C after use.
Discard the substrate if not used within 1-2 weeks.

Dilute 75 μL of BRET2 substrate into 10 mL final volume of assay buffer (resulting in a final concentration of 7.5 μM).
Load 20 μL of diluted substrate solution into each well of the cell plate using pipetting or an Integra VIAFLO liquid handler.

Spin the plates at 100 × g for 10 seconds in a table-top centrifuge.
